name: LLM-Modulo Framework
one_liner: An LLM proposes candidate plans inside a generate-test-critique loop governed by external symbolic verifiers and programmatic constraint critics.

loop.proposes: Candidate multi-day travel itineraries or symbolic plans generated by an LLM
loop.judged_by: A bank of external model-based verifiers and programmatic critics checking format, hard budget and scheduling rules, and commonsense constraints
loop.steers: A meta-controller passes the critics' critiques to the model as the next prompt until all hard critics sign off.

headline_result: Proposed at ICML 2024 (arXiv:2402.01817) and evaluated on the TravelPlanner benchmark (arXiv:2405.20625), pairing GPT-4-Turbo with external programmatic constraint critics in a bi-directional loop raised the final all-constraints pass rate from 4.4% (direct prompting) to 20.6% (a 4.6x gain), and raised GPT-3.5-Turbo from 0% to 5.0%.
caveat: Even with external critics, 20.6% leaves nearly four out of five complex multi-constraint itineraries unsolved within the retry budget, because critique-guided local edits can still fail when constraints interact globally without an exact solver.
beyond_harness_note: The LLM-Modulo loop rejects LLM self-verification in favor of sound external model-based verifiers that gate acceptance and drive iterative back-prompting.
algorithmic_authority: External symbolic verifiers (VAL for PDDL) and programmatic hard-constraint and commonsense critics

sources.title: LLMs Can't Plan, But Can Help Planning in LLM-Modulo Frameworks (ICML 2024)
Robust Planning with LLM-Modulo Framework: Case Study in Travel Planning

verification.notes: Verified against Kambhampati et al., ICML 2024 (arXiv:2402.01817) and Gundawar et al. (arXiv:2405.20625). Confirmed GPT-4-Turbo TravelPlanner final pass rate rising from 4.4% baseline to 20.6% (4.6x) and GPT-3.5-Turbo rising from 0% to 5%.
